summary:
Grammar freshness and the AST layer, checked at Yggdrasil release/6.1.0 tip 76f2701f. Every grammar package is at its latest npm release, and ABI is not a problem: web-tree-sitter 0.27.0 still accepts parser ABI 13–15 (api.h at v0.27.0: LANGUAGE_VERSION 15, MIN_COMPATIBLE 13), and all 16 shipped wasms report ABI 14 or 15 and load. The real problems are elsewhere: several grammars have stalled upstream, some fixes exist only as GitHub releases that npm never received, and some ERROR recovery drops declarations or changes edges.

Per package: pinned range → lock/installed version → latest npm → newer upstream → what the trial showed.
- web-tree-sitter: ^0.27.0 → 0.27.0 (host and lock) but 0.26.12 in the container's /workspaces → 0.27.0. Clean scratch on 0.27.0 passes 1357/1357 relation/ast/structure tests. 1884 real files give identical trees on 0.26.12 and 0.27.0.
- tree-sitter-c: 0.24.1 → 0.24.1. GitHub-only v0.24.2 (ABI 15, same node types). Trial passes. Still errors on #embed and _BitInt.
- tree-sitter-c-sharp: 0.23.5 → 0.23.5. C# 14 support exists only on master. Trial: 1 palette case fails.
- tree-sitter-cpp: 0.23.4 (Nov 2024) → 0.23.4. 41 unreleased commits on master (modules, deducing this, ABI 15). Trial passes and fixes most C++20/23 errors.
- tree-sitter-go: 0.25.0 → 0.25.0. Current.
- tree-sitter-java: 0.23.5 (Dec 2024) → 0.23.5. No grammar change since.
- tree-sitter-javascript: 0.25.0 → 0.25.0. Current, except `import defer`.
- tree-sitter-json: 0.24.8 → 0.24.8. Master fixes `1e+5`.
- tree-sitter-php: 0.24.2 → 0.24.2. Master has an ABI 15 regeneration plus PHP 8.4/8.5 fixes. Trial passes.
- tree-sitter-python: 0.25.0 → 0.25.0. Master has a breaking change (feat!): `expression_statement` becomes a supertype.
- tree-sitter-ruby: 0.23.1 (Nov 2024) → 0.23.1. Master fixes a heredoc overflow in the scanner that crashes the parse (reproduced).
- tree-sitter-rust: 0.24.0 → 0.24.0 on npm. GitHub-only v0.24.2 (ABI 14→15) fixes Rust 2024 `unsafe extern`. Trial passes.
- tree-sitter-typescript: 0.23.2 (Nov 2024, ABI 14, built on JS 0.23) → 0.23.2. No newer release upstream.
- @tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-kotlin: 1.1.0 → 1.1.0. This fork has been dormant since 2025-01. The original fwcd repo is active but unpublished and has different node types. Trial: 37 failures.
- @tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-toml: 0.7.0 → 0.7.0. The TOML 1.1.0 spec is tagged and its new forms parse as ERROR.
- @tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-yaml: 0.7.1 → 0.7.1 on npm. GitHub-only v0.7.2. Trial passes.

How the wasms ship: tsup onSuccess copies the prebuilt .wasm and node-types.json out of each npm devDep (require.resolve) into dist/grammars. Nothing is vendored or built from source. The only hash pinning is package-lock integrity, and the registry's commit and CLI pin fields are empty.

Trials ran in container scratch dirs: $TMPDIR/grammars-src (baseline), $TMPDIR/grammars-up (the C, Rust and YAML GitHub-release wasms), and $TMPDIR/grammars-headcli (C#, C++ and PHP master, plus fwcd Kotlin HEAD, all built with tree-sitter-cli 0.27.0). About 20 probe palette cases went through the real runCase pipeline, plus one live-CLI project, $TMPDIR/grammars-rb. The two big copies and the wasi-sdk cache the build downloaded (<container home>/.cache/tree-sitter, 940M) were deleted afterwards.

surviving.title: Kotlin 2.2+ syntax swallows the rest of the file into one ERROR node, so later declarations vanish. Imports of them get no edge, and an ambiguous silence can turn into one arbitrary edge
surviving.where: @tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-kotlin 1.1.0 (dist/grammars/tree-sitter-kotlin.wasm); source/cli/src/relations/extractors/kotlin.ts declarations(); palette reference/relations/kotlin/kotlin-context-parameter-type-silent.md
surviving.evidence: Parse of `package com.acme.payments / import ... / val tpl = $$"price: $$amount" / class PaymentService / class Other` gives `ERROR "val tpl = $$...\nclass PaymentService" [2:0-5:0]`, so every declaration from that line to EOF sits inside the ERROR node. When guards (`is String if x.isEmpty() ->`) and `context(log: Logger)` do the same. Probe cases through runCase on 0.27.0: zz-kt-guard-in-target-decl, zz-kt-multidollar-in-target-decl and zz-kt-context-in-target-decl all fail with `expected edge src/c/Use.kt:2->pay not emitted (got none)`. The importing file's own import survives (zz-kt-*-user-import pass). The declaring file's classes do not. False-positive check: zz-kt-guard-flips-ambiguity (the kotlin-same-fqn-two-files-ambiguous-silence layout, plus a when-guard above `class Thing` in src/x) fails with `unexpected cross-node edge src/z/Use.kt:2->y`. That breaks the matrix header's 'ZERO false positives' invariant. The realistic trigger is KMP expect/actual, where the same FQN lives in 2 files. No stable Kotlin grammar fixes this (see GF-9).
surviving.impact: Kotlin 2.2 features (guards, multi-dollar strings) and 2.4 context parameters are stable and common. One such line anywhere above a class removes that class from the SymbolTable. Every import of it from other nodes then silently yields no dependency, and the relation check passes code it never saw. Deterministic rules that walk class_declaration also miss those classes. The palette documents only the local 'type ref invisible' effect, not the loss of declarations for the whole file.
surviving.suggested_fix: In kotlin.ts, add an ERROR-tolerant declaration fallback. When a top-level ERROR node exists, re-scan its token children for `class|object|interface|typealias|fun` + identifier at depth 0, or re-parse the ERROR's byte range after the offending statement. Alternatively, mark the file 'declarations incomplete' and silence every resolution that would bind into, or disambiguate through, that file (fail-closed rather than flipping an ambiguity to an edge). Add the three zz-kt cases and the ambiguity-flip case to the palette as traps.
surviving.verifier: I reproduced this on the shipped kotlin wasm with web-tree-sitter 0.27.0 ($TMPDIR/verify-grammars-wts/probe2.mjs). The line `val tpl = $$"price: $$amount"` produces `ERROR [2:0-5:0]`, and that node contains both following classes. A when-guard and `context(log: Logger)` each produce one ERROR that runs to EOF. The control file with a plain `"a${s}"` string parses cleanly. Live CLI, pay/Pay.kt declaring PaymentService and c/Use.kt importing it: with no relation declared, the control fails with `relation-undeclared-dependency c/Use.kt:2 → pay`. The $$, guard and context variants each report `yg check: PASS` ($TMPDIR/verify-grammars-k0..k3), so a real dependency goes undetected. Ambiguity flip: the kotlin-same-fqn-two-files-ambiguous-silence layout passes, but after a when-guard is added above `class Thing` in src/x the check fails with `src/z/Use.kt:2 → y` ($TMPDIR/verify-grammars-kamb-guard). That is a false edge, against the matrix's 'ZERO false positives' invariant (kotlin-name-resolution-matrix.test.ts:24). The palette case kotlin-context-parameter-type-silent.md documents only the local type-ref gap, not the loss of every declaration to the end of the file. kotlin.ts declarations() walks only DECLARATION_TYPES nodes, so nothing inside an ERROR is keyed. Both a missed dependency and a wrong edge are reproducible.

surviving.title: Valid Ruby with a heredoc delimiter over 255 chars traps the wasm scanner. The cached parser stays broken, and yg check fails every Ruby file with a wrong 'reinstall the CLI' fix
surviving.where: tree-sitter-ruby 0.23.1 scanner.c serialize() (fixed upstream in ad907a69 on 2026-03-09, unreleased); source/cli/src/ast/parser.ts parserCache (one Parser per wasm, never reset); source/cli/src/relations/pass.ts:334-340 comment; source/cli/src/core/check-lock-phase.ts:213-218
surviving.evidence: On web-tree-sitter 0.27.0 with the shipped wasm, a heredoc delimiter of 250 chars parses ok. Delimiters of 300, 600, 1100 and 5000 chars all make parse THROW `resolved is not a function`. After that, the same Parser throws on `class Foo; end`. A new Parser, or a TS parser, still works. Live CLI project $TMPDIR/grammars-rb has app/a_long.rb (300-char delimiter), app/b.rb (`require_relative "../lib/foo"`) and lib/foo.rb. It yields `relation-parse-failed: Could not load the Ruby parser to check dependencies for 3 Ruby files, e.g. app/a_long.rb: resolved is not a function ... Fix: Reinstall the CLI`. The upstream diff changes the word-size byte `(char)heredoc->word.size` to a uint32 and fixes the off-by-one bounds check.
surviving.impact: One unusual but valid file blocks yg check for the whole repo and names the wrong cause. The fail-closed behavior is right, but pass.ts assumes 'tree-sitter never throws on bad syntax, so any throw is infrastructure'. That assumption is false for scanner memory bugs, and the same poisoning applies to any language's scanner trap. PHP master also carries an unreleased heredoc UB fix (8b7d0627).
surviving.suggested_fix: In parseFile, on a throw, evict parserCache and langCache for that wasm (optionally reload once and retry). Report a per-FILE parse failure that names the file, instead of a per-language 'could not load parser … reinstall'. Ship the ruby master scanner fix, which needs a wasm built from source (see GF-4). Add a regression case with a 300-char heredoc delimiter.
surviving.verifier: The mechanism reproduces on 0.27.0 with the shipped ruby wasm ($TMPDIR/verify-grammars-wts/rb.mjs). Delimiters of 250 and 255 chars parse. 256 and 300 chars throw `resolved is not a function`. After that, the same Parser throws on `class Foo; end`, while a fresh Parser works. Live CLI $TMPDIR/verify-grammars-rb reports `relation-parse-failed: Could not load the Ruby parser to check dependencies for 3 Ruby files, e.g. app/a_long.rb: resolved is not a function … Fix: Reinstall the CLI`. The comment in pass.ts:334-340 does assume a throw always means an infrastructure fault. The upstream fix ad907a69 ('scanner: fix heredoc serialization buffer overflows', 2026-03-10) exists, and npm is still at 0.23.1. One evidence detail is wrong: a 1100-char delimiter did NOT throw for me, so the trigger depends on the length mod 256 rather than simply 'over 255'. I downgraded it because the trigger is a heredoc identifier of 256+ characters, which real code essentially never contains. It fails closed rather than passing wrong code. What remains is a bad message and cache poisoning on a pathological input.

surviving.title: The C# extension-block palette edge passes only because 0.23.5 misparses it. The next c-sharp release (C# 14 on master) drops the edge
surviving.where: reference/relations/csharp/csharp-extension-receiver-type.md; source/cli/src/relations/extractors/csharp.ts; tree-sitter-c-sharp master (9150f7d, 'feat: C# 14 language support (#429)', 2026-06-02, unreleased)
surviving.evidence: On shipped 0.23.5, `static class Ext { extension(Widget source) { ... } }` parses as `constructor_declaration identifier "extension" parameter_list(parameter ...)` with members as local_function_statement. The edge comes from an ordinary constructor parameter. With master built via tree-sitter-cli 0.27.0, the same code becomes `extension_declaration ( receiver_parameter(identifier "Widget", identifier "source") ) extension_body(method_declaration)`. Trial suite on master: 1368 pass / 4 fail. The C# failure is `case csharp-extension-receiver-type: expected edge src/c/Use.cs:2->n not emitted (got none)`. The other 3 are the GF-1 Kotlin probes. Node-types diff 0.23.5→master: added extension_body, extension_declaration, receiver_parameter, slice_pattern; lvalue_expression gains conditional_access_expression. On 0.23.5 the probe also shows C# 14 `a?.B = 1;` → `ERROR "(A a) { a?.B"` and an expression-bodied member in an extension block → `ERROR "=> s.Length"`.
surviving.impact: When dependabot bumps c-sharp, edges from C# 14 extension blocks disappear with no code change. Only this one palette case would catch it. Until then, members inside extension blocks are misparsed as local functions, so nothing declared inside them gets indexed.
surviving.suggested_fix: Wire `extension_declaration > receiver_parameter` (and its type child) into csharp.ts usage-site walking now, keeping the constructor-shaped fallback. Add an AST-shape assertion to the case so the grammar dependency is explicit. Plan the c-sharp bump as its own migration, not a grouped devDep bump.
surviving.verifier: The facts reproduce. On shipped 0.23.5, `extension(Widget source) {…}` parses as `constructor_declaration identifier "extension" parameter_list(parameter)`, and its members parse as local_function_statement / local_declaration_statement. I built c-sharp master 9150f7d with tree-sitter-cli 0.27.0 ($TMPDIR/verify-grammars-cs/cs-master.wasm). It yields `extension_declaration > receiver_parameter(identifier Widget, identifier source) > extension_body(method_declaration, property_declaration)`, and `a?.B = 1` parses without error. csharp.ts:669 handles only `node.type === 'parameter'`. In a live CLI copy with the master wasm swapped in ($TMPDIR/verify-grammars-dist), the palette layout goes from `FAIL … src/c/Use.cs:2 → n` to `PASS`, so the edge is lost. I downgraded it because shipped behaviour is correct today, and the regression needs an unreleased grammar. The bump would also not be silent: the finding itself says csharp-extension-receiver-type's runCase fails, which turns CI red on the dependabot PR. What remains is latent fragility and a missing explicit receiver_parameter handler.

surviving.title: The build pipeline can only take wasms from npm packages, so fixes released only on GitHub never ship: rust 0.24.2 (Rust 2024 `unsafe extern`), c 0.24.2, yaml 0.7.2
surviving.where: source/cli/tsup.config.ts GRAMMARS + findFile() (require.resolve of `${pkg}/package.json`); source/cli/package.json devDependencies
surviving.evidence: npm view: tree-sitter-rust latest 0.24.0 (2025-04-01), tree-sitter-c latest 0.24.1, @tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-yaml latest 0.7.1. GitHub releases with .wasm assets: rust v0.24.2 (2026-03-27), c v0.24.2 (2026-04-22), yaml v0.7.2 (2025-10-07). On shipped rust 0.24.0, `unsafe extern "C" { fn abs(x: i32) -> i32; }` gives 2 ERROR nodes. v0.24.2 gives 0; only the `safe fn` qualifier still errors. Rust 2024 edition makes `unsafe` mandatory on extern blocks. Trial ($TMPDIR/grammars-up with those three release wasms swapped in): 1357/1357 existing tests pass, all probes pass except the unrelated Kotlin ones, rust ABI goes 14→15, and node-types.json is unchanged for all three.
surviving.impact: Every Rust 2024 crate with FFI has ERROR nodes around its extern blocks, which deterministic rules see. A `use` after the block still edges (probe zz-rs-unsafe-extern-then-use passes), so relations are fine today. Dependabot will never offer these fixes, because they do not exist on npm.
surviving.suggested_fix: Allow a grammar to come from a pinned GitHub release asset (URL + sha256) or from a source build (repo + commit + tree-sitter CLI version) in tsup.config.ts. This is exactly what the empty `grammarCommit` and `treeSitterCliVersion` registry fields were meant for. Take rust v0.24.2, c v0.24.2 and yaml v0.7.2 now: the trial shows zero regressions.
surviving.verifier: tsup.config.ts findFile() resolves wasms only via `require.resolve(`${pkg}/package.json`)`, so it can only take files from npm tarballs. npm view shows tree-sitter-rust 0.24.0 (2025-04-01), tree-sitter-c 0.24.1 and @tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-yaml 0.7.1. GitHub has releases with .wasm assets for rust v0.24.2 (2026-03-27), c v0.24.2 (2026-04-22) and yaml v0.7.2 (2025-10-07). On shipped rust, `unsafe extern "C" { fn abs(x: i32) -> i32; }` gives `function_signature_item … ERROR "{"` plus `ERROR "}"` (ABI 14). The downloaded v0.24.2 wasm gives `foreign_mod_item` with hasError false (ABI 15), and a following use_declaration is intact in both. Relation edges are unaffected. I kept major because Rust 2024 edition requires `unsafe extern`, so this is a stale grammar that misparses the current edition in deterministic-rule trees, and a ready fix exists that the pipeline cannot take. I did not re-run the 1357-test trial.

surviving.title: The TypeScript grammar is frozen at 0.23.2 (Nov 2024, ABI 14, built on JS 0.23). `using` is silently misparsed, and TS 5.x forms parse as ERROR, with no newer release anywhere
surviving.where: tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2 (dist/grammars/tree-sitter-typescript.wasm, tree-sitter-tsx.wasm)
surviving.evidence: GitHub: last tag v0.23.2 (2024-11-10); only LICENSE, FUNDING and docs commits since (HEAD 2025-01-30). package.json depends on tree-sitter-javascript ^0.23.1, while the JS grammar went to 0.25.0 (2025-09-01, which added `using` declarations). The same `using res = open();` parses in .js as `using_declaration > variable_declarator`. In .ts it parses with NO error as `expression_statement > assignment_expression(using "using", identifier "res", =, call_expression)`. Probe ERRORs on shipped TS: `import defer * as heavy from "./heavy"` → ERROR "defer" (TS 5.9); `export type * from "./types"` → ERROR "type" (TS 5.0); `interface State<in out T>` → ERROR "out T" (TS 4.7). Relations hold up: zz-ts-import-defer emits its edge; `export type *` is silenced by the ERROR-text guard in typescript-export-type-star-reexport-silence; an import after the variance error still edges.
surviving.impact: The main language of most adopters gets wrong trees for everyday TS 5.x code, and deterministic rules written against node-types.json misfire. For example, a rule looking for variable declarations never sees `using` in .ts files, yet does see it in .js. The export-type-star guard depends on the exact ERROR text, so it breaks as soon as a grammar ever models the form.
surviving.suggested_fix: Document in writing-deterministic-aspects that the TS grammar predates TS 5.0 and list the known misparses. Consider building tree-sitter-typescript from source against JS 0.25 (it is `require('tree-sitter-javascript/grammar')`-based) with a pinned CLI, which would at least bring `using_declaration`. Add palette/AST canaries for `using`, `import defer` and `export type *` so a future grammar change flips visibly.
surviving.verifier: On shipped TS, `using res = open();` parses without error as `expression_statement > assignment_expression(using "using", identifier res, …)`. The shipped JS wasm (ABI 15) gives `using_declaration > variable_declarator`. `import defer * as heavy` → ERROR "defer"; `export type * from` → ERROR "type"; `interface State<in out T>` → ERROR "out T". GitHub: latest release v0.23.2 (2024-11-11), HEAD 75b3874e 'Include LICENSE file' (2025-01-30). The package.json on master depends on tree-sitter-javascript ^0.23.1, while JS v0.25.0 was released 2025-09-01. One claim is overstated: isWholeStatementTypeToken (typescript.ts:77-79) accepts either an ERROR with text 'type' or a direct anonymous `type` token. A future grammar that models `export type *` like `export type {}` would therefore still be guarded, not broken. 'Everyday TS 5.x code' is also a stretch for `in out` and `import defer`. I kept major because the rubric names a stale grammar that misparses current language versions, and `using` / `export type *` are current TS forms.

surviving.title: The dev container's installed deps disagree with the lockfile, so the live CLI and in-container tests run web-tree-sitter 0.26.12 and vitest 4 instead of 0.27.0 and vitest 5
surviving.where: the development container, source/cli/node_modules (installed 2026-09-04); source/cli/package-lock.json (0.27.0, bumped in 6cc0c592c on 2026-09-06)
surviving.evidence: Container: node_modules/web-tree-sitter/package.json version 0.26.12, and node_modules/.package-lock.json dated 2026-09-04 lists 0.26.12. Lockfile and host have 0.27.0. `npm ls --depth=0` in the container reports as invalid: web-tree-sitter@0.26.12 (^0.27.0), vitest@4.1.11 (^5.0.0), @vitest/coverage-v8@4.1.11, vite@8.0.16, eslint@10.8.1, @clack/prompts@1.7.0, ignore@7.0.6, typescript-eslint@8.67.0, @types/node@26.2.0, @playwright/test@1.62.1. dist/bin.js imports web-tree-sitter externally, so the live CLI runs 0.26.12. Partial reassurance: a clean `npm ci` scratch on 0.27.0 passes 1357/1357 relation/ast/structure tests, and `rootNode.toString()` hashes of 1884 real files (src, tests, vitest, eslint and grammar packages, 32 of them with errors) are identical under 0.26.12 and 0.27.0.
surviving.impact: Release-loop verification done in the container does not test the toolchain CI and npm users get. Here it happened to be harmless, but the next runtime or test-runner bump could diverge silently.
surviving.suggested_fix: Run `npm ci` in the container workspace after lockfile changes (a post-merge hook or loop step). Add a guard, such as `npm ls --depth=0` exiting non-zero in the loop's preflight, so the environment cannot drift from the lock.
surviving.verifier: In the container, node_modules/web-tree-sitter is 0.26.12 and vitest is 4.1.11, and node_modules/.package-lock.json is dated Sep 4. The lockfile pins web-tree-sitter 0.27.0 and vitest 5.0.0 (bump 6cc0c592, 2026-09-06). `npm ls --depth=0` lists all 10 packages invalid as claimed. dist/bin.js imports `from "web-tree-sitter"` externally, so the live CLI runs 0.26.12. I downgraded it because this is dev-container hygiene, not a product defect. The finder's own corpus diff found identical trees, and the Kotlin, Ruby and C# behaviours I checked reproduce identically on 0.27.0 in my scratch install.

surviving.title: A grammar or runtime upgrade does not re-verify stored deterministic verdicts, and the AST facts cache key ignores the web-tree-sitter version
surviving.where: source/cli/src/core/pair-hash.ts header ('CLI version — upgrading Yggdrasil must not cascade re-verification'); source/cli/src/relations/pass.ts:417 facts key = content hash + language + grammar wasm hash + extractor rev
surviving.evidence: DetHashInput covers aspectId, scope, nodePath, ruleHash (check.mjs bytes), files and touched. No grammar wasm hash or CLI version goes in. The relation facts cache does include grammarWasmHash, but it does not include the web-tree-sitter version. 0.27.0 changes error recovery ('fix(parser): nest error children during recovery', 'restart recovery for invalid tokens in the error state', 'accumulate error costs through hidden error nodes'), though my corpus diff found no tree change.
surviving.impact: A check.mjs verdict recorded under the old grammar stays 'verified' after a yg upgrade whose new grammar would make the same rule return a different result. Examples: the C# 14 extension parse in GF-3, and python master hiding `expression_statement` as a supertype. Keyless CI stays green on stale results until the code changes. The facts cache is speed-only and re-resolves live, so a runtime-only change there is low risk.
surviving.suggested_fix: Fold the grammar wasm hash of each subject file's language into DetHashInput. That is narrower than the CLI version and invalidates only the pairs whose parse input changed. Add the web-tree-sitter version to factsKey for completeness.
surviving.verifier: DetHashInput (pair-hash.ts:55-57) extends CommonHashInput, which holds aspectId, scope, nodePath, ruleHash, files and verdict, plus touched. The observation kinds (pair-hash.ts:270-276) are read, list, exists, graph*, config, node-files and graph-files. None covers the grammar or AST. fill-det.ts:255-263 passes exactly these fields. grammarWasmHash is used only in relations/pass.ts. The header deliberately excludes the CLI version, but nothing addresses grammar bytes. A grammar change (for example the C# master extension parse I observed) could therefore leave a stale deterministic verdict in place. Minor is right.

surviving.title: Upstream breaking node-type changes are queued, and dependabot will send them grouped as harmless 'minor' devDep updates
surviving.where: .github/dependabot.yml (groups dev-dependencies: update-types [minor, patch]); tree-sitter-python master 26855ea; tree-sitter-cpp master; tree-sitter-php master
surviving.evidence: python master commit 'feat!: mark `expression_statement` as a supertype' makes supertypes hidden, so user rules matching `expression_statement` stop matching. Node-types diff v0.25.0→master: added tuple_expression, expression_statement gains subtypes. cpp master has 'feat!: add support for reflection (P2996)' and an ABI 15 regeneration. php master has 'feat!: regenerate with ABI 15 and `Array` aliasing changes'. All of these arrive as 0.x minor bumps (0.25→0.26 and so on). dependabot.yml groups minor with patch, and its own comment says majors are kept separate because they break things. For 0.x grammars, though, the breaking changes are the minor bumps. Trial on cpp and php master: all tests pass. On C# master: 1 palette case fails (GF-3).
surviving.impact: A grammar upgrade that breaks users' deterministic rules or silently shifts extractor inputs can land inside a routine grouped PR. The palette catches only relation-side effects, and nothing guards the node-types contract that rule authors are told to rely on.
surviving.suggested_fix: Exclude tree-sitter-* and @tree-sitter-grammars/* from the grouped updates (their own group or ungrouped). Add a node-types.json snapshot test per grammar so any rename, removal or supertype change is an explicit reviewed diff, and publish grammar changes in the CHANGELOG as rule-author-facing.
surviving.verifier: .github/dependabot.yml groups dev-dependencies with `update-types: [minor, patch]`, and its comment separates only majors. All tree-sitter grammars are 0.x devDependencies, so a 0.25→0.26 bump is classed as 'minor'. Upstream breaking commits exist: python 26855eab 'feat!: mark `expression_statement` as a supertype'; cpp c95a0b14 'feat!: add support for reflection (P2996)' and 80f5bd82 'regenerate with ABI 15'. The palette would still catch relation-side breaks in CI, so this is process risk for deterministic-rule authors only. Minor.

surviving.title: The Kotlin grammar source is split: the fork yg ships is dormant, and the active upstream is unpublished and has different node types
surviving.where: package.json @tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-kotlin ^1.1.0; github.com/fwcd/tree-sitter-kotlin
surviving.evidence: tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-kotlin: last release v1.1.0 (2025-01-09), a single CI commit since. fwcd/tree-sitter-kotlin (the original, npm `tree-sitter-kotlin`) is active through 2026-08-02: 'Multi-dollar string interpolation (#260)', 'Added guard condition in when-expression (#256)', KEEP-0438 destructuring. surviving.evidence: Live $TMPDIR/tsprobe-misc: src/c/pkg/package.json `{"main":"./lib/main.ts"}` and `import { Y } from '../c/pkg'` → no edge to c (yg check PASS). `#internal/x` is silenced by the palette's design.
surviving.impact: Node.js subpath imports (`#…`) are becoming the recommended replacement for tsconfig paths in NodeNext projects, and they and in-repo packages with `main` or `exports` go undetected.
surviving.suggested_fix: When resolving a directory, or a `#` specifier, read the nearest package.json's `main`, `exports` or `imports` (conditions import/default/types) and re-enter the candidate probing. This shares its implementation with TS-6.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced in $TMPDIR/verify-typescript-js-ts89. src/c/pkg/package.json is `{"main":"./lib/main.ts"}` and `import { Y } from "../c/pkg"` gives no edge to c, while the control `import … from "../g/value"` gives `use.ts:5 → g`. candidates() in typescript-resolve.ts:42-71 probes only index.* for directories. `#internal/x` is a documented palette silence (typescript-package-subpath-imports-silence). surviving.title: Vite/bundler forms are missed: a root-absolute `/src/...` specifier is joined onto the importer's directory, and `?raw`, `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` and import.meta.glob are not recognised
surviving.where: src/relations/extractors/typescript-resolve.ts resolveTsPath (`path.posix.join(baseDir, specifier)` also for '/'-prefixed specifiers); typescript.ts (no new URL or import.meta.glob handling)
surviving.evidence: Live $TMPDIR/tsprobe-misc from src/a/use.ts: `import { X } from '/src/b/value'` (would resolve to src/a/src/b/value), `import r from '../e/raw.ts?raw'` (extname '.ts?raw' → probes 'raw.ts?raw.ts'), and `new Worker(new URL('../d/worker.ts', import.meta.url))` → yg check PASS with no edges to b, d or e.
surviving.impact: Vite projects with root-absolute imports, query-suffixed imports or worker URLs silently lose edges. The '/' join also means that a nested child node mapped under the importer's directory could in principle receive a wrong edge.
surviving.suggested_fix: Resolve '/'-prefixed specifiers against the project or package root, not the importer's directory, or silence them explicitly. Strip `?query` and `#hash` suffixes before probing. Consider `new URL('<literal>', import.meta.url)` as an edge. Catalogue all of these as cases.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced in $TMPDIR/verify-typescript-js-ts89. `import { V } from "/src/b/value"`, `import r from "../e/raw.ts?raw"` and `new Worker(new URL("../d/value.ts", import.meta.url))` produce no edges to b, d or e, while the control to g works. typescript-resolve.ts:29 joins '/'-prefixed specifiers onto the importer's directory. I also confirmed the wrong-edge variant in a legal, non-overlapping config: in $TMPDIR/verify-typescript-js-ts9m, node a maps src/a/use.ts, node n maps src/a/src/b and node b maps src/b. `import … from "/src/b/value"` then reports `src/a/use.ts:1 → n` instead of b. That setup is contrived, so minor stands.

surviving.title: Re-export with import attributes mis-parses in every grammar and the statement disappears
surviving.where: grammars tree-sitter-typescript/tsx/javascript: `export ... from ... with {…}`
surviving.evidence: The AST for `export { X } from '../b/v' with { type: 'json' };` in the TS grammar is `(program (labeled_statement label: (statement_identifier) (ERROR (export_clause …) source: (string …)) body: …) (ERROR) (empty_statement))`, with no export_statement. Probe: javascript also gives ERROR for `export { x } from './b.json' with {`. The palette only covers the `import … with` form, which parses fine.
surviving.impact: Today this matters little, because the targets are JSON or CSS, which the resolver never treats as source candidates. It becomes a real miss if JSON or asset edges are ever added (TS-12), and it is a silent grammar hole.
surviving.suggested_fix: Add a palette case for `export {…} from … with {…}` that pins the current behaviour. Fix it through the grammar vendoring in TS-7.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced in $TMPDIR/verify-typescript-js-ts10. `export { X } from "../b/v" with { type: "json" };` pointing at a .ts file gives no edge, and the next import still gives `use.ts:2 → c`. The TS parse dump is `labeled_statement@1 / ERROR "}" / empty_statement`, with no export_statement. The probe confirms ERROR in typescript, tsx and javascript. The palette covers only `import … with`. The hole is local and real targets are usually JSON, so minor.

surviving.title: Imports from Vue/Svelte SFCs and JSON data files are invisible
surviving.where: src/utils/language-registry.ts (no .vue/.svelte/.astro); typescript-resolve.ts (never probes .json/.vue/.svelte targets)

summary:
Python + Ruby, release/6.1.0 @ 76f2701f. Grammars: tree-sitter-python 0.25.0 and tree-sitter-ruby 0.23.1 are both npm latest (npm view). Python 0.25.0 already parses 3.12 PEP 695/701, 3.14 t-strings (PEP 750) and unparenthesised except (PEP 758). The one Python syntax gap is PEP 696 defaults, and upstream master lacks it too. tree-sitter-ruby has had no release since Nov 2024. Master carries an unreleased heredoc scanner fix (ad907a6, 2026-03-10), and without it the shipped wasm crashes. Palette is 1:1 with tests (python 22 md / 22 runCase, ruby 19 / 19).

Python covered and correct: plain, aliased and multi import; from-import with the submodule candidate; relative sibling and parent; star; conditional, function-local and TYPE_CHECKING imports; PEP 420 namespace submodules (also relative inside a namespace package, live P7); re-export to __init__. Deliberate silences: __future__, importlib, the namespace package object, stdlib/external, relative escape, __all__.

Ruby covered: require_relative, top-level superclass, include/extend/prepend, qualified values and receivers, rooted ::X, compact class, assignment RHS, pattern-match constants. Deliberate silences: plain require, const_get/autoload, reopening ambiguity, compact reopened external, a bare constant inside a class or module body.

Live tests used scratch projects $TMPDIR/pyrb-* in the container with `yg check --no-approve`. Ground truth came from python3.13 in the container. The container has no Ruby, so Ruby lookup semantics come from Module.nesting and the docs. Worst results:
- Python: absolute-import resolution probes the importer's own and intermediate package dirs, so a stdlib or third-party import shadowed by an ancestor module (logging, celery) gives a false edge. src-layout tests and uv-workspace cross-package imports are silently missed.
- Ruby: the forms Rails code uses most (bare constant in a method body, bare superclass inside a module, Zeitwerk implicit namespaces) are all silent. A qualified ref inside a namespace can bind the wrong node. Nested reopenings of gem namespaces (ActiveRecord::Base) and core_ext reopenings (String) give false edges. A heredoc delimiter of 256+ chars crashes the Ruby wasm, which poisons the cached parser and fails every Ruby file with a misleading "Could not load the Ruby parser / reinstall" message.

Environment note: the dev container's node_modules has web-tree-sitter 0.26.12, not the locked 0.27.0. I re-ran the grammar and crash probes against a fresh web-tree-sitter@0.27.0 in $TMPDIR/pyrb-wts and got identical results.

surviving.title: Ruby heredoc delimiter of 256+ chars crashes the shipped Ruby wasm; the cached parser is poisoned so every later Ruby file fails with a misleading 'Could not load the Ruby parser / reinstall' error
surviving.where: tree-sitter-ruby 0.23.1 src/scanner.c (serialize/deserialize heredoc word length as uint8); source/cli/src/ast/parser.ts:38 (parserCache per extension); source/cli/src/relations/pass.ts:331-357; source/cli/src/core/check-lock-phase.ts:213-218
surviving.evidence: Direct probe with shipped dist/grammars/tree-sitter-ruby.wasm: delimiter length 250 → ok; 256/300/1030 → 'THROW TypeError: resolved is not a function' at web-tree-sitter.js stubs.<computed> (an unresolved wasm import stub called from the scanner). The same Parser then throws on 'x = Foo::Bar' ('after THROW'), while a fresh Parser parses it fine. Same result on web-tree-sitter 0.27.0 ($TMPDIR/pyrb-wts). Live $TMPDIR/pyrb-r10 (lib/a/aa_first.rb has a 256-char heredoc, lib/a/zz_use.rb has 'y = Flag', lib/b/flag.rb): yg check → 'relation-parse-failed: Could not load the Ruby parser to check dependencies for 3 Ruby files, e.g. lib/a/aa_first.rb: resolved is not a function … Fix: Reinstall the CLI'. The real a→b edge is never computed. Upstream fix ad907a6 ('scanner: fix heredoc serialization buffer overflows', 2026-03-10) widens word length to uint32 and fixes the bound. It is not in any npm release (0.23.1 is latest). The pass.ts comment assumes any throw is a grammar-load fault ('tree-sitter … never throws on bad syntax').
surviving.impact: A single pathological file blocks relation conformance (and any ctx.parseAst aspect) for the whole Ruby codebase, and the remedy it prints (reinstall) cannot help. The trigger itself is rare, but the containment failure is general: any external-scanner trap in any grammar has the same blast radius.
surviving.suggested_fix: On a parse throw, evict the parserCache entry, retry once on a fresh Parser, and report the failure against that one file ('parser crashed on <file>') rather than as a grammar-load failure. Build tree-sitter-ruby.wasm from master ≥ ad907a6 (or vendor the patched scanner) until npm ships a release. Add a regression case with a 256-char heredoc delimiter.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. In $TMPDIR/verify-python-ruby-r1, with lib/a/aa_first.rb holding a heredoc whose delimiter is 256 'A's, yg check prints 'relation-parse-failed: Could not load the Ruby parser to check dependencies for 3 Ruby files, e.g. lib/a/aa_first.rb: resolved is not a function … Fix: Reinstall the CLI'. That is 3 files, so the cached parser also takes down zz_use.rb and b/flag.rb. With a 255-char delimiter the real edge 'a lib/a/zz_use.rb:1 → b' comes back. npm view tree-sitter-ruby gives version 0.23.1 (last modified 2024-11-11). gh shows upstream commit ad907a6 'scanner: fix heredoc serialization buffer overflows' from 2026-03-10, and there is no tag after v0.23.1. pass.ts:340-346 does assume that any throw is a grammar-load fault. I downgraded it because the trigger (a heredoc delimiter of 256 or more characters) essentially never occurs in real code, and the check fails closed and loudly rather than passing with wrong edges. The real defects are the misleading 'reinstall' remedy and the poisoned parserCache (parser.ts:38): robustness problems, not a common-code blocker. Side note: language-registry.ts sets ruby `externalScanner: false`, although tree-sitter-ruby has an external scanner.

surviving.title: Python false edge: a stdlib or third-party import binds to an in-repo module of the same name in an ancestor package directory
surviving.where: source/cli/src/relations/extractors/python-resolve.ts:99-120 (resolveAbsolute probes every ancestorDirs() entry, including dirs that are themselves inside a package)
surviving.evidence: $TMPDIR/pyrb-p3: app/__init__.py, app/logging.py (node base), app/api/routes.py 'import logging' (node api) → yg check FAIL 'api app/api/routes.py:1 → base'. Ground truth in the same dir: python3 -c 'import app.api.routes as r; print(r.logging.__file__)' → /usr/lib/python3.13/logging/__init__.py. $TMPDIR/pyrb-p3b (canonical Django+Celery layout): proj/celery.py, proj/orders/tasks.py 'from celery import shared_task' → 'orders proj/orders/tasks.py:1 → proj', listed twice. The palette's python-stdlib-import-silence fixture only has an unrelated billing/charge.py decoy and never tests an ancestor-dir shadow.
surviving.impact: A false positive that blocks CI and has no waiver. Module names like logging.py, celery.py, email.py, redis.py or types.py are common at the top of an app package, and every import of the real library from a sub-package then produces a false edge.
surviving.suggested_fix: A directory that contains __init__.py is inside a package and is not a sys.path root. Only probe ancestor dirs that are not regular-package dirs (the dir holding the importer's top-level package, plus repo root / src / configured roots). Add the palette case python-stdlib-shadowed-by-ancestor-module-silence (logging.py / celery.py).
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. In $TMPDIR/verify-python-ruby-p1b (app/__init__.py and app/logging.py in node base, app/api/routes.py 'import logging' in node api), yg check FAILs with 'api app/api/routes.py:1 → base'. python3 in the same dir resolves r.logging.__file__ to /usr/lib/python3.13/logging/__init__.py. The cause is python-resolve.ts:98-117: it probes every ancestorDirs() entry, including package-internal dirs, and a single match is returned as an edge. No palette case covers an ancestor-dir shadow; python-stdlib-import-silence only has an unrelated billing/charge.py. One claim is overstated. The 'canonical Django+Celery layout' only fires when the app sits inside proj/ ($TMPDIR/verify-python-ruby-p1c: 'orders proj/orders/tasks.py:1 → proj'). In the documented sibling layout (orders/ next to proj/, $TMPDIR/verify-python-ruby-p1d) the check PASSes with no false edge. It stays major because a top-level package with a logging/types/email/redis module and sub-packages under it is a common shape, and the false edge blocks CI.

surviving.title: Python recall gap: imports across source roots (tests/ → src/ layout, uv/poetry workspace members) are silently missed
surviving.where: source/cli/src/relations/extractors/python-resolve.ts:99 (roots = ancestors of the importing file only)
surviving.evidence: $TMPDIR/pyrb-p1: src/core/service.py (node core), tests/test_service.py 'from core.service import run' (node tests) → yg check PASS, no edge. Ground truth: PYTHONPATH=src python3 → core.service $TMPDIR/pyrb-p1/src/core/service.py. $TMPDIR/pyrb-p2: packages/lib/src/lib/util.py (node lib), packages/api/src/api/main.py 'from lib.util import helper' (node api) → PASS, no edge. Neither src/ nor packages/lib/src is an ancestor of the importer.
surviving.impact: The PyPA-recommended src layout (for tests) and uv/Poetry workspaces (for cross-package imports) are mainstream today. In both, the cross-node dependencies the graph most needs to police go undetected.
surviving.suggested_fix: Discover source roots repo-wide: every dir containing pyproject.toml/setup.cfg, its src/ child, uv [tool.uv.workspace] members, and setuptools/hatch package dirs. Probe them in addition to the ancestor roots and keep the 2+-distinct-match ambiguity rule. Add palette cases python-src-layout-tests-edge and python-workspace-member-edge.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. $TMPDIR/verify-python-ruby-p2 (src/core/service.py in node core, tests/test_service.py 'from core.service import run' in node tests) gives PASS with no edge. $TMPDIR/verify-python-ruby-p2b (packages/api/src/api/main.py 'from lib.util import helper' against packages/lib/src/lib/util.py) also gives PASS with no edge. The control $TMPDIR/verify-python-ruby-p2c, with the importer moved under src/, gives 'tests src/tests/test_service.py:1 → core'. The only roots are the importer's ancestors (python-resolve.ts:98), and nothing in docs/ or the palette documents this limitation. The tests→src half matters less, since tests are usually allowed to depend on src. Missing cross-member imports in uv/Poetry workspaces is a real, undocumented gap on a mainstream layout.

surviving.title: Ruby wrong-node edge: a qualified but unrooted constant inside a namespace is treated as absolute, but Ruby resolves its first segment lexically
surviving.where: source/cli/src/relations/extractors/ruby.ts:65-73 (isCompleteReference treats any scope_resolution as shadow-free) and :222; palette reference/relations/ruby/ruby-qualified-mixin-edge.md ('qualified `Shared::Loggable` is shadow-free')
surviving.evidence: $TMPDIR/pyrb-r2: lib/billing/invoice.rb 'module Billing; class Invoice' (node billing); lib/shop/billing/invoice.rb 'module Shop; module Billing; class Invoice' (node shopbilling); lib/shop/cart/cart.rb 'module Shop; class Cart; def checkout; Billing::Invoice.new' (node cart) → yg check 'cart lib/shop/cart/cart.rb:4 → billing'. Ruby looks up `Billing` through Module.nesting [Shop::Cart, Shop] first, finds Shop::Billing, and the code really uses Shop::Billing::Invoice (node shopbilling). Only a `::`-rooted ref is absolute. Corollary: if only Shop::Billing::Invoice exists, the same ref is silenced, because root `Billing` is unanchored (resolver.ts:128-132).
surviving.impact: Wrong-target edge, which is a false positive for billing and a missed dependency for shopbilling. Namespaced Rails and gem code (Api::V1, Admin::…) regularly references sibling namespaces partially qualified.
surviving.suggested_fix: Treat only `::`-rooted refs as complete. For `A::B` inside nesting [N1, N2, …], build candidates N1::A::B, N2::A::B, …, A::B and resolve through the existing resolveCandidateGroup, taking the first present and silencing on ambiguity. Fix the palette text and add ruby-qualified-ref-lexical-shadow-silence / -edge cases.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. In $TMPDIR/verify-python-ruby-r2 (lib/billing/invoice.rb defines Billing::Invoice, lib/shop/billing/invoice.rb defines Shop::Billing::Invoice, and lib/shop/cart/cart.rb has 'module Shop; class Cart; def checkout; Billing::Invoice.new'), yg check gives 'cart lib/shop/cart/cart.rb:4 → billing'. The cause is ruby.ts:69-72: isCompleteReference returns true for every scope_resolution, rooted or not, and the ruby-qualified-mixin-edge palette text calls an unrooted `Shared::Loggable` 'shadow-free'. That is wrong under Ruby semantics: the first segment of an unrooted A::B is looked up lexically through Module.nesting, so the real target is Shop::Billing::Invoice. Ruby is not installed in the container, so I could not run the runtime check. The Module.nesting rule is standard documented Ruby behaviour. The result is a wrong-target edge that breaks the zero-false-positive invariant.

surviving.title: Ruby false edge: a nested reopening of a gem namespace (module ActiveRecord; class Base) anchors the root, so ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base binds to the initializer
surviving.where: source/cli/src/relations/resolver.ts:128-132 (rubyRootUnanchored only catches the compact form); ruby.ts declarations() :250-303
surviving.evidence: $TMPDIR/pyrb-r4: config/initializers/ar_ext.rb 'module ActiveRecord\n  class Base\n    def self.soft_delete!; end' (node init); app/models/application_record.rb 'class ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base' (node models) → yg check FAIL 'models app/models/application_record.rb:1 → init'. The palette's ruby-reopened-external-constant-silence covers only the compact form `module Rack::Handler`.
surviving.impact: A false positive that blocks CI in the most common Rails file (ApplicationRecord). Nested monkey-patches of ActiveRecord, ActiveSupport or ActionController in initializers or lib/ are common.
surviving.suggested_fix: Do not treat a reopening as an anchor for binding. Require corroboration that the in-repo definition creates the constant: the file path matches the Zeitwerk/gem convention for the FQN (…/active_record/base.rb), or the root is not a known external namespace. Add palette case ruby-reopened-external-nested-silence.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. In $TMPDIR/verify-python-ruby-r3, config/initializers/ar_ext.rb reopens ActiveRecord::Base in nested form ('module ActiveRecord\n  class Base …') and app/models/application_record.rb has 'class ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base'. yg check FAILs with 'models app/models/application_record.rb:1 → init'. The nested `module ActiveRecord` records the single-segment key 'ActiveRecord', so rubyRootUnanchored (resolver.ts:128-132) treats the root as anchored. The palette's ruby-reopened-external-constant-silence covers only the compact `module Rack::Handler` form. The result is a false edge in the most common Rails file, and nested monkey-patches in initializers are common.

surviving.title: Ruby false edge: a core_ext reopening of a builtin (class String) makes every top-level use of String bind to the core_ext node
surviving.where: source/cli/src/relations/extractors/ruby.ts:222 (bare constant emitted at nsDepth 0) with the declarations() indexing of `class String`
surviving.evidence: $TMPDIR/pyrb-r5: lib/core_ext/string.rb 'class String\n  def shout = upcase + "!"' (node coreext); spec/formatter_spec.rb 'RSpec.describe "formatter" do … expect(String.new("a"))' (node specs) → yg check FAIL 'specs spec/formatter_spec.rb:3 → coreext'. RSpec describe blocks, rake tasks, config/routes and initializers all run at nsDepth 0, so every bare constant in them is emitted.
surviving.impact: Apps with lib/core_ext reopenings of String/Hash/Array/Time/Object get false edges from every spec and top-level script that mentions those classes.
surviving.suggested_fix: Never bind Ruby core and stdlib constants (String, Hash, Array, Integer, Object, Kernel, Time, Date, Struct, …) to in-repo reopenings, and treat them as absent. More generally, apply the same reopening-is-not-definition rule as RB-3. Add palette case ruby-core-class-reopening-silence.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. In $TMPDIR/verify-python-ruby-r4, lib/core_ext/string.rb reopens String, and spec/formatter_spec.rb (top-level RSpec.describe block) calls 'expect(String.new("a"))'. yg check FAILs with 'specs spec/formatter_spec.rb:3 → coreext'. At nsDepth 0 a bare constant is emitted (ruby.ts:222), and the single in-repo `class String` is its unique definition. The declarations() doc comment (ruby.ts:244-248) assumes a reopening shows up as 2+ files, which does not hold when there is only one reopening file. core_ext reopenings are common in Rails and gem code, so these false edges show up regularly.

surviving.title: Ruby recall gap: bare constants inside class/module bodies, the dominant Rails dependency form, are always silenced
surviving.where: source/cli/src/relations/extractors/ruby.ts:172 (superclass suppressed when nsDepth>0), :202 (mixins suppressed when nsDepth>1), :222 (bare constant suppressed when nsDepth>0); palette ruby-lexical-shadowing-bare-silence
surviving.evidence: $TMPDIR/pyrb-r1: app/models/order.rb 'class Order'; app/controllers/orders_controller.rb 'class OrdersController < ApplicationController; def index; @orders = Order.where(open: true)' → yg check PASS, no controllers→models edge. $TMPDIR/pyrb-r7: 'module Admin\n  class UsersController < ApplicationController' with ApplicationController in another node → PASS, no edge.
surviving.impact: In a Zeitwerk app nearly every cross-component dependency (model use in controllers, services and jobs, and base classes under a namespace) is a bare constant inside a class body. The Ruby relation check therefore misses most real dependencies, and it catches the rest only from top-level code or `Foo::Bar` refs.
surviving.suggested_fix: Resolve through lexical candidates instead of blanket suppression. For bare X in nesting [A::B, A], build candidates A::B::X, A::X, X via resolveCandidateGroup, and emit only when every nested candidate is absent from the SymbolTable and X is unique. summary:
Go + Rust relation extraction and grammar freshness on Yggdrasil release/6.1.0 (76f2701f). I read all 12 Go and 14 Rust palette cases, both matrix test files, go.ts/go-resolve.ts, rust.ts/rust-resolve.ts and the go.mod/Cargo.toml discovery in resolve-path.ts (makeGoResolveDeps/makeRustResolveDeps). I then ran 16 scratch projects in the container ($TMPDIR/gr-*, built from $TMPDIR/gr-lib/mk.mjs, `yg check --approve --only-deterministic`) and parsed the newest-syntax files with the shipped dist/grammars wasm ($TMPDIR/gr-lib/parse.mjs, which drives the CLI's own web-tree-sitter).

What the palette covers:
- Go (edges): single, grouped, raw-string, aliased, blank and dot imports.
- Go (silenced): stdlib, external module, go.work, replace, unmapped package, intra-package.
- Rust (edges): `use crate::`, alias, grouped with a common prefix, glob, `pub use`, file-backed `mod foo;`, inline `crate::`/`self::`/`super::` paths in type and expression position.
- Rust (silenced): bare-root inline path, external crate, `#[path]`, inline mod body, macro token trees.

These baseline forms work live. Go generics, cgo `import "C"`, `internal/` and a `/v2` module all behaved correctly in the scratch project.

The sharpest problems are in Rust:
1. Grouped `use crate::{a::X, b::Y}` (the rustfmt/rust-analyzer merged-import style) produces no edge at all.
2. Groups with nested sub-paths bind to the prefix module's node.
3. Inline `mod tests { use super::*; }` resolves `super` from the file rather than from the inline module, which produces a false edge.
4. Items defined in lib.rs are never reachable.
5. `src/bin/*.rs` and `tests/*.rs` are treated like `src/` modules. That gives one wrong-node edge and misses `mod` edges.
6. Multi-module Go (go.work, nested module to parent) and Rust workspace path dependencies are silent everywhere. These are deliberate recall gaps, but they remove exactly the edges a module-per-node monorepo cares about.

Grammars:
- tree-sitter-rust: npm latest is 0.24.0 (shipped), but upstream tagged v0.24.1 and v0.24.2 on GitHub in March 2026 without publishing them to npm. One of those fixes, `unsafe extern` blocks (required in edition 2024), fails to parse in the shipped wasm.
- tree-sitter-go: 0.25.0 (shipped) is still the latest; the last grammar commit was September 2025. Go 1.26 `new(expr)` and Go 1.27 generic methods both give ERROR nodes, and there is no upstream fix.
- Relation extraction survives these ERROR nodes (tested live). Rules that use ctx.parseAst do not.
- web-tree-sitter 0.27.0 is current and the wasm loads fine (no ABI problem).

surviving.title: `super`/`self` inside an inline `mod tests { use super::*; }` resolves relative to the FILE, which creates a false edge to the parent module's node

Any file at depth ≥2 whose parent module file belongs to a node outside its ancestor chain gets a spurious relation-undeclared-dependency. The same bug affects `self::` inside inline modules, and `mod foo;` declared inside an inline `mod outer { … }`, which really lives at `<dir>/outer/foo.rs`.

Either consume one leading `super` per enclosing inline mod before calling the resolver (`super` inside 1 inline mod means the file's own module), or prepend the inline-mod names to `self::` specifiers. surviving.title: Items defined in the crate root (lib.rs/main.rs) are unreachable: `use crate::{Config, Error}` / `crate::Error` resolve to nothing

npm view tree-sitter-rust: `"version": "0.24.0"`, latest. `git ls-remote --tags` lists `refs/tags/v0.24.1` and `refs/tags/v0.24.2` (tagged 2026-03-27). surviving.verifier: npm view tree-sitter-rust gives version 0.24.0 (dist-tag latest). git ls-remote shows refs/tags/v0.24.1 and v0.24.2, and the GitHub commits API dates the v0.24.2 commit 2026-03-27. grammar.js at v0.24.2:283-284 has `foreign_mod_item: seq(optional('unsafe'), $.extern_modifier, …)`, where v0.24.0:281-282 has `optional($.visibility_modifier)`. dist/grammars/tree-sitter-rust.wasm has the same sha256 (f65f3542…) as node_modules 0.24.0. Relation extraction is unaffected, so the impact is limited to parseAst/file.ast rules on FFI files. It still fits the rubric's 'stale grammar that mis-parses current language versions'.

surviving.title: Shipped tree-sitter-go 0.25.0 mis-parses Go 1.26 `new(expr)` and Go 1.27 generic methods; upstream has no newer release
surviving.where: source/cli/package.json `"tree-sitter-go": "^0.25.0"`; dist/grammars/tree-sitter-go.wasm
surviving.evidence:
npm view tree-sitter-go gives 0.25.0 (latest, published 2025-08). Upstream HEAD 2346a3a (2025-09-15) has only CI commits since v0.25.0.
Release notes: go.dev/doc/go1.26 says "The built-in new function … now allows its operand to be an expression". go.dev/doc/go1.27 says "Go 1.27 now supports generic methods".
Live parse with the shipped wasm: `func P() *int { return new(42) }` gives `ERROR L20: "42"`. `func (r *Rand) N[Int ~int | ~int64](n Int) Int { return n }` gives `ERROR L6: "func (r *Rand) N[Int ~int | ~int64](n Int) Int"`.
Generic type aliases (1.24), `range n`, range-over-func, self-referential constraints (1.26) and 1.27 selector keys in struct literals parse clean. Imports still resolve ($TMPDIR/gr-go-internal-cgo-generics: `app m/cmd/app/main.go:9 → store`).
surviving.impact: The current Go release (1.27, August 2026) produces ERROR subtrees for generic method declarations. goExtractor.declarations() loses those methods, and parseAst-based rules see a broken tree. Import-based relation detection is unaffected because imports precede the broken code.
surviving.suggested_fix: No upstream grammar fix exists. Either carry a patched grammar (add type_parameters to method_declaration; let `new` take an expression) and build the wasm in-repo, or document the known limitation and add a freshness fixture that flags it. File or track the issue upstream in tree-sitter/tree-sitter-go.
surviving.verifier: npm view tree-sitter-go gives 0.25.0 (latest). The upstream commits API shows only CI bumps since the 2025-08-29 '0.25.0' commit, so there is no fix to bump to. go.dev/doc/go1.27 (line 456) says 'Go 1.27 now supports generic methods', and go1.26 (line 456) says new's operand may be an expression. go.dev/dl lists go1.27.1 as current. The shipped wasm parses `func (r *Rand) N[Int ~int | ~int64](n Int) Int {…}` with `ERROR L5`, and `return new(42)` with `ERROR L3: "42"`. Generic aliases and range-over-int parse clean. Imports and relations are unaffected, and Go declarations() is only a 'thin parity layer'. The impact is on parseAst rules, and the fix needs a patched grammar, not a version bump. Major fits the rubric, but the item is a limitation to document or patch, not a stale dependency.

surviving.title: Edition-2024 raw identifiers (`mod r#gen;`, `use crate::r#gen::X`) resolve to `r#gen.rs`, so the dependency is silently missed
surviving.where: source/cli/src/relations/extractors/rust.ts pathText / mod_item emit (use the raw `.text`, including the `r#` prefix); rust-resolve.ts probes `<seg>.rs` verbatim

surviving.suggested_fix: Strip a leading `r#` from every path segment and mod name before emitting (the file-name rule). Add palette case rust-raw-identifier-module-edge.
surviving.verifier: The mod_item emit (rust.ts:261) and pathText (rust.ts:81/93) use the raw .text, including `r#`, and the resolver probes `r#gen.rs`. Live in $TMPDIR/verify-go-rust-rs6 (edition 2024): lib.rs `pub mod r#gen;` and app.rs `use crate::r#gen::Generated;` give only `root r/src/lib.rs:1 → app`, and both edges to node gen are missing. summary:
Java, Kotlin and C# on release/6.1.0 (76f2701f). I read every palette case in reference/relations/{java,kotlin,csharp}, the extractors (java.ts, java-resolve.ts, kotlin.ts, csharp.ts), resolve-path.ts, symbol-table.ts and resolver.ts. I parsed the newest syntax of each language with the shipped grammar .wasm files (dist/grammars, via web-tree-sitter, from $TMPDIR/jkc-probe/parse.mjs). I then ran about ten small two-node projects through `yg check --no-approve` in the container ($TMPDIR/jkc-*).

**Grammar versions.** All four packages are at their npm latest: tree-sitter-java 0.23.5 (2024-12-21), tree-sitter-c-sharp 0.23.5, @tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-kotlin 1.1.0 (2025-01-09) and web-tree-sitter 0.27.0. None of the three language grammars fully covers its current language version:
- **C#:** upstream HEAD has unreleased C# 14 support (#429, 2026-06-02).
- **Kotlin:** the shipped grammar has no fix upstream. The fwcd fork has when-guards and multi-dollar strings on main, but they are unreleased.
- **Java:** upstream has no commits since the tag except CI and license changes.

**Java.** Imports, static and wildcard imports, and inline fully-qualified names are well catalogued. One structural recall hole remains: import resolution only searches the importing file's own directory and its parents. So nothing crosses Maven/Gradle module roots, and src/test cannot reach src/main.

**Kotlin.** It loses edges in five ways:
- Wildcard imports are always silenced.
- Java↔Kotlin imports never resolve, because the symbol table is per-language.
- When two files in the same node declare the same name (KMP expect/actual, overloads spread across files), the name counts as ambiguous and is silenced.
- Local `val`/`fun` declarations inside functions are indexed as if they were top-level names.
- The stale grammar turns everything after a when-guard or a context parameter into one ERROR node, which erases the rest of the file.

**C#.** It has three false-positive or wrong-target mechanisms:
- `global using` is aggregated repo-wide, with no .csproj scoping.
- Global aliases collide last-wins across projects.
- The file-based ambiguity rule silences partial classes and `Result`/`Result<T>` split across files.

Its recall holes: in-repo generic types (`Repository<T>`, `IHandler<,>`) are never an edge, static member access through a type name is never detected, and composition-root extension calls are missed.

All findings below were reproduced live unless stated otherwise.

surviving.title: Java imports never resolve across Maven/Gradle module roots or from src/test to src/main
surviving.where: source/cli/src/relations/extractors/java-resolve.ts:86-90 (resolveJavaPackageFiles), :95-118 (resolveType), :123-133 (ancestorDirs); dispatched from source/cli/src/relations/resolve-path.ts:63-97
surviving.evidence:
The resolver only tries `<ancestor-of-importing-file>/<fqn path>.java`. It never searches a sibling tree such as module-b/src/main/java.

Live test $TMPDIR/jkc-java-mm, nodes a=module-a/**, b=module-b/src/main/**, bt=module-b/src/test/**. A.java has `import com.app.b.B;` (line 2), `import com.app.b.*;` (line 3), `import static com.app.b.B.X;` (line 4) and a class body with `com.app.b.B fq` (line 5). Output: `- a  module-a/src/main/java/com/app/a/A.java:5 → b` only. The inline fully-qualified name fires through the SymbolTable, but all three imports are silent. BTest.java (module-b/src/test) `import com.app.a.A;` is also silent.

Live test $TMPDIR/jkc-java-test: src/test/java/com/app/t/BTest.java `import com.app.b.B;` against node b=src/main/**. Result: `yg check: PASS`, no edge.

Palette: every one of the ~100 Java fixture paths sits under a single `src/main/java/` root. No case covers multiple modules or src/test.
surviving.impact: The most common inter-component edge in real Java (module A imports module B in a multi-module Maven/Gradle build) is invisible for single, wildcard and static imports. A graph whose nodes are modules gets almost no Java recall. Only inline fully-qualified names, which are rare, fire. This is also inconsistent: the same type fires when written fully qualified inline but not when imported.
surviving.suggested_fix: When the ancestor walk misses, fall back to the Java SymbolTable (declarations() already emits `pkg.Type` / `pkg.Outer+Inner` keys): a type import resolves to the unique defining file, and a wildcard import collapses to its owner set. Alternatively, gather every source root in the repo (directories whose relative path matches the declared package) and probe each. Add palette cases java-multi-module-sibling-import-edge, java-multi-module-wildcard-edge and java-test-root-to-main-root-edge.
surviving.verifier: Code: java-resolve.ts:86-90 and :108-117 only probe `<ancestor-of-importing-file>/<fqn>.java`. Fresh repro in $TMPDIR/verify-jvm-dotnet-j1: module-a/src/main/java/com/app/a/A.java `import com.app.b.B;` plus A2.java `import com.app.b.*;`, B in module-b/src/main/java, and BTest in module-b/src/test/java `import com.app.b.B;`, with nodes a=module-a/**, b=module-b/src/main/**, bt=module-b/src/test/**. Result: `yg check: PASS`, no edges at all. Control with one root, $TMPDIR/verify-jvm-dotnet-j2 (src/main/java/com/app/{a,b}): `A.java:2 → b`. The palette has no case for multi-module or src/test layouts (grep for multi-module/source root in reference/relations turned up nothing for Java), so this is not a documented silence. A module-per-node graph in a Maven or Gradle build gets essentially no import edges, which is a missed real dependency in common code.

surviving.title: `global using` from one .csproj leaks into every C# project in the repo and creates false edges
surviving.where: source/cli/src/relations/pass.ts:561-570 (projectGlobalUsings aggregated over all C# facts); csharp.ts assembleCsharpCandidates usingPrefixes union
surviving.evidence:
Live test $TMPDIR/jkc-cs2:
- Api/Api.csproj; Api/GlobalUsings.cs `global using Api.Models;`; Api/Models/Customer.cs declares `Api.Models.Customer`.
- Worker/Worker.csproj has only `<PackageReference Include="Vendor.Crm">` and no reference to Api.
- Worker/SyncJob.cs: `using Vendor.Crm; namespace Worker; public class SyncJob { Customer _c; }`.

Output: `relation-undeclared-dependency ... - worker  Worker/SyncJob.cs:3 → api`. Worker's `Customer` comes from the external Vendor.Crm package, but Api's global using was injected into Worker's using tier, so `Api.Models.Customer` bound. No code in src reads .csproj files: `git grep -i csproj source/cli/src` returns nothing.
surviving.impact: This produces false positives that block CI in any solution with more than one project that uses `global using`, which is the default style since .NET 6 (a GlobalUsings.cs per project). The design's own rule (D8) is zero false positives with no waiver. Separately, `<Using Include="..."/>` items in .csproj, the other C# 10 way to declare global usings, are invisible.
surviving.suggested_fix: Scope global usings and global aliases to the owning project: the nearest ancestor directory containing a *.csproj. Apply a project's set only to files under that project. Parse `<Using Include>` / `<Using Remove>` from the same .csproj (and Directory.Build.props). Add palette cases csharp-global-using-other-project-no-leak (expectation silence) and csharp-csproj-using-item-edge.
surviving.verifier: Mechanism confirmed: pass.ts:560-568 unions every C# file's global usings into one repo-wide set, and nothing in src reads .csproj. Repro $TMPDIR/verify-jvm-dotnet-cs1: Api/GlobalUsings.cs `global using Api.Models;`, Worker/SyncJob.cs `using Vendor.Crm; ... Customer _c;` gives the false edge `worker Worker/SyncJob.cs:3 → api`. The claim that this hits 'any solution with more than one project that uses global using' is overstated. The false positive needs a simple-name collision where the consuming project's real binding is invisible to the tool (an external package or an SDK implicit using) and another project's global-using namespace declares that name. When both projects' names are in-repo, the effect is a spurious ambiguity (a silence), not a false edge. It is a real zero-FP breach in multi-project solutions, but it is conditional, so major.

surviving.title: `global using` aliases collide last-wins across projects, so an alias binds another project's type (wrong target node)
surviving.where: source/cli/src/relations/pass.ts:562,567 (`projectGlobalUsingAliases.set(name, fqn)` — a Map, last writer wins)
surviving.evidence:
Live test $TMPDIR/jkc-cs4:
- Billing/GlobalUsings.cs `global using Money = Billing.Model.Money;`
- Shipping/GlobalUsings.cs `global using Money = Shipping.Model.Money;`
- Billing/Invoice.cs `namespace Billing; public class Invoice { Money total; }`
- Relations declared: billing→bmodel, shipping→smodel.

Output: `- billing  Billing/Invoice.cs:2 → smodel`. Billing's `Money` resolved to Shipping.Model.Money. Which alias wins depends on file iteration order.
surviving.impact: The edge points at the wrong node. The real dependency (billing→bmodel) is never checked, and a bogus undeclared dependency blocks CI. Even without scoping, two conflicting definitions of one alias should never pick one silently.
surviving.suggested_fix: Scope aliases per .csproj (same fix as CS-01). Until then, record every target an alias name maps to. If an alias maps to more than one distinct target project-wide, treat it as ambiguous and silence it, never last-wins. Add palette case csharp-global-alias-cross-project-collision-silence.
surviving.verifier: Confirmed: pass.ts:567 `projectGlobalUsingAliases.set(name, fqn)` is last-wins, and the code comment's premise ('a genuine cross-file collision is a compile error') holds only within one project. Repro $TMPDIR/verify-jvm-dotnet-cs2 with `global using Money = Billing.Model.Money;` and `global using Money = Shipping.Model.Money;`. Output: `billing Billing/Invoice.cs:2 → smodel` (wrong target) and `shipping Shipping/Parcel.cs:2 → smodel`. It is a wrong edge, but it needs two projects to define the same global alias name with distinct in-repo targets, which is uncommon. It shares a root cause and fix with CS-01, so major rather than blocker.

surviving.title: Ambiguity is counted by distinct files, not owner nodes, so declarations split across files in the same node are silenced
surviving.where: source/cli/src/relations/resolver.ts:181 (`if (files.size !== 1) return undefined;`), :206-212 (classify); symbol-table.ts:13-16
surviving.evidence:

surviving.impact:
Several very common layouts lose every inbound edge:
- C# partial classes across files (EF, WinForms/WPF designer files, source generators, big split classes).
- The `Result`/`Result<T>`, `Entity`/`Entity<TId>`, `IRequest`/`IRequest<T>` pattern with one type per file.

Stay ambiguous only for two or more distinct owners, and handle unmapped files as today. Add palette cases csharp-partial-class-multi-file-edge, csharp-generic-arity-split-files-edge, kotlin-expect-actual-same-node-edge and kotlin-toplevel-overload-multi-file-edge. Keep a cross-node duplicate case as silence. Optionally key C# declarations with arity (`Result`1`) so `Result<int>` binds the generic declaration.
surviving.verifier: resolver.ts:182-183 silences whenever `files.size !== 1`, counting files, not owners. C# repro $TMPDIR/verify-jvm-dotnet-x1: `partial class Customer` split across Customer.cs and Customer.Validation.cs in node people, and `Result` plus `Result<T>` in separate files of node res. Uses.cs:5 (`Customer c`) and :6/:7 (`Result r`, `Result<int> ri`) give no edges. Control $TMPDIR/verify-jvm-dotnet-x1c, with the second files removed: `Uses.cs:5 → people`, `Uses.cs:6 → res`. Control k1c without jvmMain and UserMappers: `A.kt:2 → shared`, `A.kt:3 → shared`, `A.kt:4 → map`. No case covers same-node duplicates, and nothing covers C# partials. Recall is lost on very common layouts.

surviving.title: In-repo generic types are never an edge: the base name of a `generic_name` is deliberately skipped
surviving.where: source/cli/src/relations/extractors/csharp.ts emitTypeNode `case 'generic_name'` ("Descend the type arguments ONLY (the base container name is not a dependency here)"); same rule applied to base_list, fields, new, parameters
surviving.evidence:
Live test $TMPDIR/jkc-cs1:
- Node core declares `Repository<T>`, `IHandler<TReq,TRes>`.
- Node domain declares `Order`.
- App/Uses.cs (line 6) `public class OrderRepo : Repository<Order> { }` and (line 7) `public class H : IHandler<string, int> { }`.

surviving.impact: Generic abstractions are the main cross-layer contracts in modern .NET: `Repository<T>`, `IRequestHandler<TReq,TRes>` (MediatR), `Result<T>`, `Entity<TId>`, `AggregateRoot<TId>`, `IValidator<T>`. surviving.suggested_fix: For a `generic_name`, emit the base identifier as its own candidate group (same alias/enclosing-namespace/using expansion as a bare identifier) in addition to descending the type arguments. Add palette cases csharp-generic-base-class-edge and csharp-generic-interface-impl-edge, and a silence case showing `List<Foo>` gives no edge to a List container.

surviving.suggested_fix: Build a repo-wide PSR-4 index from every composer.json (skip vendor/). Resolve with the nearest map first, and if no prefix matches, fall back to the union of all maps (at least the ancestors).
